description: We’re HolySquare, a group of friends joining NASA Space Apps Almaty online. We want to use data from NASA’s Mars missions to build a map that helps astronauts plan a walk on Mars. Where does the terrain get steep? What’s worth stopping to study? We want explorers to see those trade-offs as they choose a route.
summary:
HolySquare is an interactive Mars Extravehicular Activity (EVA) simulation and intelligent expedition-planning platform designed to explore the challenges of future human missions to Mars.

Our project combines a realistic 3D Martian environment with a scientific mission planner built around real planetary terrain data from the Gale Crater region. Users can explore the Martian surface as an astronaut, operate a Perseverance rover, select scientific objectives and plan expeditions across five Curiosity-inspired research locations.

The platform evaluates multiple route alternatives while considering terrain hazards, oxygen consumption, spacesuit energy, rover battery and mission time. It also simulates unexpected situations such as dust storms, equipment failures and oxygen leaks, allowing users to experience the complexity of conducting an EVA.

By transforming real planetary observations into an interactive exploration and planning experience, HolySquare makes Mars science more accessible and demonstrates how data-driven planning can support the study of future human exploration missions.
details:
HolySquare is a browser-based Mars exploration and expedition-planning platform focused on the Gale Crater and Mount Sharp boxwork region of Mars. It consists of two interconnected experiences: a 3D Mars EVA simulation and an advanced scientific expedition planner.

The EVA simulation allows users to explore a Martian environment as an astronaut and interact with a Perseverance rover. Users must manage oxygen, spacesuit battery power, temperature and mission time while completing scientific activities and returning safely to their habitat. The simulation includes environmental events and equipment failures, such as dust storms, oxygen leaks, communication blackouts and rover faults. It also features voice commands and assisted return navigation.

The expedition planner uses real terrain information to calculate and compare multiple mission routes. It analyzes elevation, slope, roughness, rock density and terrain hazards to generate shortest, fastest, lowest-risk, science-focused and balanced alternatives. Each plan is evaluated against oxygen, suit energy, rover battery and available mission time, including the resources required for returning to base.

Our scientific objectives are inspired by five Curiosity rover research locations in the Gale Crater region. Users can select scientific activities, prioritize objectives and evaluate the feasibility of their expeditions.

The project incorporates NASA mission resources, including Mars Odyssey THEMIS infrared imagery, Curiosity mission observations and rover waypoint information. We also use USGS planetary elevation and orthophoto products derived from Mars mission observations.

Our technology stack includes React, TypeScript, Vite, Three.js, OpenLayers and Zustand. We use MediaPipe Tasks Vision for optional camera-based hand gesture recognition and Blender for 3D model development.

What makes HolySquare creative is its integration of planetary science, interactive 3D exploration, and intelligent mission planning. Rather than presenting Mars data as static maps, we transform it into a simulated environment where users experience the decisions and resource trade-offs involved in planetary exploration.

During development, we considered scientific data provenance, terrain coverage, navigation limitations, uncertainty in rover station coordinates, resource constraints, accessibility, and the distinction between real observations and hypothetical simulation parameters.

Our intended impact is to improve public understanding of planetary exploration and demonstrate how real scientific datasets can be transformed into engaging tools for studying the challenges of future human Mars missions.
